## Overview

A UBC MDS Capstone project predicting patient mortality and hospital readmission
at 1, 6, and 12 months post-discharge by fusing 3D CT imaging with structured
electronic health record (EHR) data. The project replicates and extends a
published late-fusion architecture, introducing a novel cascaded modeling approach.

---

## Dataset

The [INSPECT dataset](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-023-02737-2) —
23,248 CTPA (CT pulmonary angiography) studies from 19,402 patients, with
paired structured EHR features and longitudinal outcome labels.

---

## Architecture

### Baseline: Late Fusion (Huang et al.)

The published baseline trains a 3D CNN on CT volumes and a gradient-boosted
model on EHR features independently, then combines their output probabilities
via a learned fusion layer.

```
CT Volume ──► 3D CNN ──► p_ct ─┐
                                ├──► Fusion Layer ──► Final Prediction
EHR Features ──► GBM ──► p_ehr ─┘
```

### Our Extension: Cascaded Fusion

We proposed integrating CT diagnostic outputs *directly into the EHR feature
vector* before the EHR model trains, so the structured model sees imaging-derived
signals as features — not just as a parallel output to combine at the end.

```
CT Volume ──► 3D CNN ──► CT diagnostics ─┐
                                          ▼
                         EHR Features + CT diagnostics ──► GBM ──► Final Prediction
```

This allows the EHR model to learn interactions between imaging findings and
structured clinical data, rather than treating them as independent.

---

## Target Metric

AUROC ≥ 0.90 across all prediction horizons, validated against the partner
institution's clinical benchmarks.
